Figure 25.9 Pathophysiology of Osteoarthritis
A normal joint (left) and a joint affected by osteoarthritis (right) are compared. 
Early osteoarthritic changes shown on the left side of the affected joint include 
thickening of the articlar cartilage, narrowing of the joint space, and development 
of surface cracks in the cartilage. Late changes shown on the right side of the 
affected joint include erosion of cartilage, development of bone cysts as synovial 
ﬂ uid comes into contact with bone, and formation of osteophytes or bone spurs.
Source: CM Porth, Pathophysiology: Concepts of Altered Health Status 7e.
